title: Private Credit's Clock is Ticking w/ Glenn Schorr & Ken Worthington | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 72
summary: Glenn Schorr and Ken Worthington discuss cash-sweep economics, AI agents, private-market exits, software refinancing and crypto infrastructure. Eisman is skeptical of Schwab cash dependence, Circle competitive position and private-credit marks. The most concrete credit test remains 2027-2029 refinancing, not current redemptions alone. KKR record exits provide an acknowledged exception. Visa evidence supports incumbent competition but also shows USDC cooperation. Eisman uniform 50% private-software mark inference and broad crypto-hedge logic require stronger evidence and clearer assumptions.
assessment: Full transcript reviewed. Empirical claims without inspected primary outcome evidence remain unresolved; guest claims are separate from Eisman attribution. Primary outcome verification is incomplete for claims marked unresolved; these are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman hosts. Glenn Schorr covers large banks and alternatives; Ken Worthington covers retail brokers, exchanges, alternatives and crypto. Attribution follows explicit questions and continuity but is not an audio-verified diarization.
framework_points: Separate funding liquidity, asset cash flow and collateral valuation.
Distinguish institutional versus retail distribution and manager dispersion.
Separate blockchain utility, token value capture and exchange revenues.
Model both incumbent competition and partnership in payments.
Examine service bundling before treating cash spreads as pure customer inertia.
tools_and_charts: Sweep balances, net interest revenue and funding spreads
Wealth-channel gross sales and quarterly redemptions
Software maturity ladder and refinancing equity gap
Trading revenue versus volume and margin balances
transcript_cautions: Captions render SaaS as SAS and agentic as genetic or gentic.
Three-speaker turns are inferred from coverage and question context; individual attribution is medium confidence.
Crypto expected-direction passage contains an apparent down/down transcription or verbal contradiction.
The $20bn hedge-fund claim is unnamed and unverified.
